tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

scope.description: Required with items: "first_task", "continuation" or "new_task" (see the tool description). Omit on advance / done / start updates.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

items.description: The whole plan, in order (1–12 steps); replaces the previous list.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). ## Context

- Repository `/Users/guygouri/Devlab/ernlang/ern`, branch `reference/memory-model-v0`. Lake project `formal/`
  (Lean 4, no Mathlib). Build from `formal/` with `~/.elan/bin/lake`.

import Ern.MemoryModel.Machine
import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Preserve.Common

/-!
# Refinement of the access kernel into the elementary memory machine (spec v0, Part XVII)

Source: `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md`, §82 (items 1–8) with §10, §16, §17, §23.

* A layout of places in allocations and its interface `LayoutWF` (§82.1, §23).
* The representation relation `Repr` between a kernel state (`Access.S3`) and an admissible state
  of the memory machine (`Machine.State`, §9) (§82.1, §82.3, §82.4, §82.5).
* For every kernel operation O1–O16, the sequence of raw operations that realizes its `ok` step,
  proven to be a sequence of `ok` raw steps that keeps `Repr` (§82 preamble, §82.2, §82.4, §82.5).
* Safe reads and writes (§82.2), lifetimes (§82.5), deallocation contracts (§82.4), pinned
  addresses (§82.6), exclusivity of bytes (§82.8), pointers written by `store` (§82.3).
* A simulation of runs from the initial state with parameters fixed once per run, and concrete
  runs checked by evaluation.

The sequential fragment only (§18, §29): no theorem here says anything about concurrency.
-/

namespace Ern.MemoryModel.Refinement

open Ern.MemoryModel.Access

/-! ## Allocations of the memory machine (§9) -/

/-- The allocation `i` of `s2` is registered and satisfies `p` (§9, §11 ¶2). -/
def AllocP (s2 : Machine.State) (i : Nat) (p : Machine.Alloc → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ a, s2.allocs i = some a ∧ p a

/-- The allocation `i` of `s2` is registered and live (§9 ¶1, §17 ¶3). -/
abbrev LiveAlloc (s2 : Machine.State) (i : Nat) : Prop := AllocP s2 i (·.live = true)

/-- Weakening of the property of a registered allocation (§9). -/
theorem AllocP.mono {s : Machine.State} {i : Nat} {p q : Machine.Alloc → Prop}
    (h : AllocP s i p) (hpq : ∀ a, p a → q a) : AllocP s i q :=
  let ⟨a, ha, hp⟩ := h; ⟨a, ha, hpq a hp⟩

/-- Two properties of one registered allocation (§9). -/
theorem AllocP.and {s : Machine.State} {i : Nat} {p q : Machine.Alloc → Prop}
    (hp : AllocP s i p) (hq : AllocP s i q) : AllocP s i fun a => p a ∧ q a := by
  obtain ⟨a, ha, h1⟩ := hp
  obtain ⟨b, hb, h2⟩ := hq
  rw [ha] at hb; cases hb
  exact ⟨a, ha, h1, h2⟩

/-- A registered allocation is below the counter of a state with fresh identities (§9 ¶7). -/
theorem AllocP.lt {s : Machine.State} (hwf : Machine.WF s) {i : Nat} {p : Machine.Alloc → Prop}
    (h : AllocP s i p) : i < s.next :=
  Nat.lt_of_not_le fun hle => by obtain ⟨a, ha, -⟩ := h; rw [hwf i hle] at ha; cases ha

/-- Base address of the allocation `i` of `s2`, `0` if unregistered (§9 ¶1, §12 ¶1). -/
def baseOf (s2 : Machine.State) (i : Nat) : Nat := ((s2.allocs i).map (·.base)).getD 0

/-- The base of a registered allocation (§9 ¶1). -/
theorem baseOf_of {s2 : Machine.State} {i : Nat} {a : Machine.Alloc} (h : s2.allocs i = some a) :
    baseOf s2 i = a.base := by
  simp [baseOf, h]

/-! ## Layout of places (§82.1, §23) -/

/-- Layout of places (§82.1): place `q` occupies the range `L q` of the elementary memory machine:
an allocation identity, an offset and a length (§11 ¶1). A parameter fixed for a run, defined on
every index, present or future. Only the allocation of a non-leaf place is read. -/
abbrev Layout := Nat → Machine.Place

/-- Layout interface in the states `s3`, `s2` (§82.1; §23 "a memory layout satisfying
`LayoutWF`"). The spec names `LayoutWF` without stating its clauses; the clauses below are the
guarantees §82.1 and §23 ask the layout to provide. No lower bound on lengths: a leaf may have
size zero (§71.1). -/
structure LayoutWF (L : Layout) (s3 : S3) (s2 : Machine.State) : Prop where
  /-- §82.1 (parts): a structural part lies in the allocation of its parent. -/
  parts : ∀ q r, parentOf s3.P q = some r → (L q).alloc = (L r).alloc
  /-- §23, §82.1 (disjointness): two distinct leaves in one allocation have disjoint ranges. -/
  disjoint : ∀ l l', l < s3.P.length → l' < s3.P.length → isLeaf s3.P l → isLeaf s3.P l' →
    l ≠ l' → (L l).alloc = (L l').alloc →
    Machine.RangeDisjoint (L l).off (L l).len (L l').off (L l').len
  /-- §82.1, §15 ¶1: the range of a leaf lies within its allocation, which is registered. -/
  within : ∀ l, l < s3.P.length → isLeaf s3.P l →
    AllocP s2 (L l).alloc fun a => (L l).off + (L l).len ≤ a.size

/-- Elements of a parent chain lie in the allocation of its start (§82.1 parts, §40). -/
theorem alloc_chainF {L : Layout} {P : List Place}
    (hp : ∀ q r, parentOf P q = some r → (L q).alloc = (L r).alloc) :
    ∀ k i r, r ∈ chainF (parentOf P) k i → (L i).alloc = (L r).alloc
  | 0, _, _, h => by simp [chainF] at h
  | k + 1, i, r, h => by
    simp only [chainF] at h
    split at h
    · rename_i o ho
      split at h
      · rcases List.mem_cons.1 h with rfl | h
        · exact hp i _ ho
        · exact (hp i o ho).trans (alloc_chainF hp k o r h)
      · simp at h
    · simp at h

/-- A part lies in the allocation of every place it belongs to (§82.1 parts, §40). -/
theorem LayoutWF.alloc_part {L : Layout} {s3 : S3} {s2 : Machine.State} (hl : LayoutWF L s3 s2)
    {l r : Nat} (h : partOf s3.P l r) : (L l).alloc = (L r).alloc := by
  rcases h.2 with rfl | h
  · rfl
  · exact alloc_chainF hl.parts l l r h

/-! ## Representation relation (§82.1, §82.3, §82.4, §82.5, §9) -/

/-- Representation relation between a kernel state `s3` and a state `s2` of the memory machine,
for the layout `L` and the deallocation tokens `rtok` recorded for the allocation of each root
place (`rtok r` for the root place `r`; §17 ¶4, §70.2):
- `adm`: `s2` is admissible (§9 ¶8: freshness, live disjointness, alignment);
- `layout`: the layout interface (§82.1, §23);
- `inj`: two distinct root places are in distinct allocations (§82.1: storage units and
  identities; §9 ¶5: subplaces are not new allocations, so parts share their root's);
- `tokens`: the allocation of a root place is registered and records the token `rtok r`
  (§82.4, §17 ¶4);
- `live`: the allocation of a usable root place is live (§82.5);
- `init`: the bytes of the range of an `Init` leaf are initialized (§82.3; `Uninit` and `Moved`
  impose nothing, §41).
It does not read the contract `K` (§48). -/
structure Repr (L : Layout) (rtok : Nat → Nat) (s3 : S3) (s2 : Machine.State) : Prop where
  /-- §9 ¶8: admissibility of the memory state. -/
  adm : Machine.Admissible s2
  /-- §82.1, §23: layout interface. -/
  layout : LayoutWF L s3 s2
  /-- §82.1, §9 ¶5: distinct root places, distinct allocations. -/
  inj : ∀ r r', RootPlace s3.P r → RootPlace s3.P r' → r ≠ r' → (L r).alloc ≠ (L r').alloc
  /-- §82.4, §17 ¶4: the allocation of a root place is registered with the token `rtok r`. -/
  tokens : ∀ r, RootPlace s3.P r → AllocP s2 (L r).alloc fun a => a.freeAuth = some (rtok r)
  /-- §82.5: the allocation of a usable root place is live. -/
  live : ∀ r, RootPlace s3.P r → s3.Usable r → LiveAlloc s2 (L r).alloc
  /-- §82.3: the range of an `Init` leaf is initialized. -/
  init : ∀ l, l < s3.P.length → isLeaf s3.P l → s3.I l = .init →
    AllocP s2 (L l).alloc fun a => a.InitRange (L l).off (L l).len

# ERN — Memory Model Specification v0.1

**Edition v0.1 — corrective candidate, not yet validated**

Modified clauses, relative to v0 (each change is justified by a defect found while formalizing v0):

- §36: `MetaRight` governs authorities over existing storage, not the fresh allocation of `alloc`; §36 and §71.2 contradicted each other.
- §40: `RootHeld` restricted to usable root places, as in §49.7; the two clauses differed on unusable root places.
- §47: the ownership graph of statics is acyclic; a static ownership cycle made §57 false in the initial state.
- §51: a valid origin is an active origin; "valid" was undefined there.
- §57: definition of I5, which v0 named without defining.
- §59: "access operations" are O9–O11; read as all operations, §59 contradicted §69.
- §60.1: a valid origin chain is an active one, read through §44.
- §63.4: the active derived authorities covering the source from outside are named, and the authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right are exempt; without this exemption no value could be moved through a derived authority.
- §63.9 (new): the destination is usable in the resulting state; without it an accepted transfer could create an ownership cycle and break §49.8 and §57.
- §69.2 and §70.3: the same exemption as §63.4, and rejection when an authority made inactive by the step keeps an active descendant; without it an accepted step left an active authority with an inactive origin.
- §71.2: the provider is a usable place; v0 did not require it to exist.
- §74 and §75: each `pin` installs an obligation of fresh identity and `unpin` ends one designated obligation; per-leaf pin flags let an `unpin` lift a pin installed by another `pin`.
- §76.6: the reading of the precondition (whole kernel state, `ArenaInv` of the new entry, resulting state); v0 admitted several readings with different verdicts.
- §78.3: restricted to anchors covering a leaf of the administered storage; as written, its second sentence was false.
- §82.2: address and provenance of a pointer to a region whose leaves all have zero physical size; v0 decided no address for that region.
- §86: the last sentence is rewritten; as written, it was false, since `reset` and `issue` leave a recycled leaf `Init` and readable.

**Higher normative authority:** *ERN — Language Charter v0* (October 27, 2026).  
This specification defines the normative rules of ERN's memory model. Technical names (`derive`, `transfer`, `issue`, etc.) designate **abstract semantic operations**; they do not constitute syntax decisions.

## Validation and Revision Procedure

This edition has been validated and acquires normative authority under the ERN Charter v0. Any subsequent semantic change must identify the clauses concerned, justify the change, and preserve the guarantees of the ERN Charter v0. Formal models and proofs are instruments for verifying this specification, not sources of additional rules. Behaviors not determined within its scope are explicitly identified.

## Scope

This specification defines:

- the safe-code contract;
- the abstract machine for allocations, bytes, and accesses;
- the second-class access discipline;
- footprints, authorities, dependencies, frames, and ownership;
- read, write, transfer, release, allocation, and pinning transitions;
- the normative contract of arenas as a reference library abstraction;
- the correspondence obligations between these mechanisms.

It does not define syntax, the complete concurrency model, control-flow conventions, the type system, or compiler lowering. The sequential model's scope does not waive the general guarantees of the Charter.

---

# I. Safe-Behavior Contract

The following contract applies to all safe code and all properly encapsulated abstractions, regardless of their concrete memory representation.

## 1. Definitions of Safe Behavior

**Safe operation:** An operation that imposes no unchecked safety obligation on its user whose violation could compromise the language's guarantees.

**Safe code:** Code that executes only safe operations and does not directly assume obligations specific to unsafe operations.

**Safe interface:** An interface whose every permitted use preserves the language's guarantees when its implementation is correct.

**Safe abstraction:** An abstraction exposing a safe interface; its implementation may use unsafe operations provided it fulfills all their obligations.

# XIII. Pinning, Statics, and External Commitments

Pinning forbids certain movements or ends of lifetime. It is not a general guarantee of content immutability.

## 74. O15 — Dynamic Pinning

**Preconditions:** `place` is usable, the current frame has exercisable `Modify` over the relevant leaves, and the operation respects applicable pinning obligations.

**`ok` effect:** A dynamic pinning obligation of fresh identity is installed on the relevant leaves. A leaf is dynamically pinned while at least one active pinning obligation covers it. While an obligation is active, `transfer`, `endUse`, `free`, and `exitFrame` are rejected if they act on leaves it pins; removal of this obligation requires `unpin` under `K.ExternalDone`. Pinning does not make contents immutable. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 75. O16 — Removal of Dynamic Pinning

**Preconditions:** `unpin` designates one active dynamic pinning obligation, installed by `pin` on `place`; `place` is usable, the current frame has exercisable `Modify`, and contract `K.ExternalDone`, applied to that obligation, attests that all relevant external use has ended.

**`ok` effect:** The designated dynamic pinning obligation ends, and only that one: a leaf it covered stays pinned while another active obligation covers it. The step does not itself modify values, their initialization, or their access authorities. Static obligations are not removed by this operation. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

**Associated static rule (`StaticPinnedBottom`):** Statics designated by `K.Pinned` must be places **directly** owned by the **base frame**, not merely transitively owned by a static value. This restriction ensures that they do not die when an intermediate frame exits.

# XIV. Arenas and Collective Invalidation — Reference Abstraction

An arena is a **library abstraction**, not a memory-kernel primitive. Operations O17 through O19 are **derived** from operations O1 through O16 and abstraction-specific metadata: `newArena` registers an administration without modifying the kernel; `issue` performs `split` followed by `store` (after checking availability); `reset` performs a `Modify` derivation over all storage—through `derive` or `split`—then `release`, before restoring availability. Their contract below is **normative for the standard-library arena** until Spec 10 takes responsibility for it. It authorizes neither new permissions nor an additional access machine. Arena entries (Section 46) constitute the abstract state of this administration; the guard in Section 56 belongs to its consistency contract. The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and are not defined here.

----
# XVII. Correspondence Between Access Discipline and Memory Machine

A transition of the access discipline must admit a realization compatible with the bytes and allocations of the memory machine. An abstract definition of a right does not suffice to justify its concrete representation.

## 82. Representation Relation and Concrete Obligations

1. **Places and bytes:** relate `P`, `footprint` leaves, their ownership, and their parts to the storage units, offsets, ranges, identities, and alignment constraints of the elementary memory machine; establish actual disjointness for `DeclaredDisjoint` declarations.
2. **Authorities and operations:** connect effective modes and `ExercisableAt` to concrete read, write, and pointer-validity conditions; show that safe access governed by Parts VI through XV satisfies the obligations of Part III, without conflating ownership and binary representation. A pointer to a region whose leaves all have zero physical size is represented like a pointer to the empty region: its address is the base of the allocation of the effective anchor of its authority, and that allocation is its provenance.
3. **Initialization:** relate `Uninit`, `Init`, and `Moved` to concrete values and representations; an authority `store` must correspond to writing an actual reference into **a single logical leaf** with an appropriate representation.
4. **Allocation and deallocation:** relate `alloc` / `free` to `AllocStep` / `DeallocStep`, justify `Satisfiable`, `Deallocable`, and `FreeCompat`, as well as the zero-physical-size case.
5. **Lifetimes:** relate `endUse`, `exitFrame`, `NoDangling`, dependencies, and death markers to the validity effects on actual storage.
6. **Pinning and static storage:** prove compatibility of permitted moves and pinned-address restrictions; specify the physical obligations of statics and external use. Hardware-specific MMIO semantics remain outside the sequential kernel.
7. **Arenas:** show that the library abstraction's derived operations and metadata, distinct from `S₃`, can be realized by operations O1–O16; relate issued regions and local/static/allocated storage to the elementary memory machine without reintroducing access after invalidation.
8. **`noalias`:** infer no pointer-lowering property from abstract invariants alone; memory justification is established here and the translation choices at Spec 13 level.

# XVIII. Examples of Semantic Behavior
----
## 87. Pinning an In-Place Value

A pinned in-place leaf cannot be physically moved by `transfer`. If only an allocation owned by a value is pinned, transfer of that value may remain valid when the other conditions hold, because the owned allocation is not physically moved.

142	/-- Effect of an `ok` raw operation (§20.2): a read leaves the state unchanged. -/
143	def opEff : Machine.Op Ty → Machine.State → Machine.State
144	  | .read _ _, s => s
145	  | .write ac _ w, s => s.write ac w
146	  | .dealloc id _, s => s.dealloc id
147	  | .alloc sp b sz al fa, s => s.alloc sp b sz al fa
148	
149	/-- State after a sequence of `ok` raw operations (§20.3 ¶3). -/
150	def run : Machine.State → List (Machine.Op Ty) → Machine.State
151	  | s, [] => s
152	  | s, o :: os => run (opEff o s) os
153	
154	/-- `p s o` holds for each operation `o` of the sequence in the state where it runs (§20.3). -/
155	def Along (p : Machine.State → Machine.Op Ty → Prop) :
156	    Machine.State → List (Machine.Op Ty) → Prop
157	  | _, [] => True
158	  | s, o :: os => p s o ∧ Along p (opEff o s) os
159	
160	/-- Decidability of `Along` for a decidable property (§20.3 ¶3). -/
161	instance decAlong (p : Machine.State → Machine.Op Ty → Prop) [h : ∀ s o, Decidable (p s o)] :
162	    (s : Machine.State) → (os : List (Machine.Op Ty)) → Decidable (Along p s os)
163	  | _, [] => isTrue trivial
164	  | s, o :: os => @instDecidableAnd _ _ (h s o) (decAlong p (opEff o s) os)
165	
166	/-- The parametric obligations of a raw read or write hold, both parts (§15 ¶5, §16 ¶4,
167	§20.3 ¶1): explicit predicates of the execution context, never replaced by `True`. -/
168	def Obl (ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty) (ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty) (s : Machine.State) :
169	    Machine.Op Ty → Prop
170	  | .read ac t => ObR.dec s ac t ∧ ObR.stat s ac t
171	  | .write ac t w => ObW.dec s ac t w ∧ ObW.stat s ac t w
172	  | _ => True
173	
174	/-- The parametric obligations hold for every read and write of a sequence, in the state where it
175	runs (§20.3). -/
176	abbrev OblAlong (ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty) (ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty) :
177	    Machine.State → List (Machine.Op Ty) → Prop :=
178	  Along (Obl ObR ObW)
179	
180	/-- The operation is an `ok` raw step from `s` to its effect (§20.1 ¶2). -/
181	def OkAt (C : Nat → Nat → Prop) (ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty) (ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty)
182	    (s : Machine.State) (o : Machine.Op Ty) : Prop :=
183	  Machine.Step C ObR ObW o s (opEff o s)
184	
185	/-- A sequence of operations each `ok` where it runs is an execution (§20.3 ¶3). -/
186	theorem exec_of_along {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty}
187	    {ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty} :
188	    ∀ (os : List (Machine.Op Ty)) (s : Machine.State), Along (OkAt C ObR ObW) s os →
189	      Machine.Exec C ObR ObW os s (run s os)
190	  | [], s, _ => .nil s
191	  | _ :: os, _, ⟨h, hs⟩ => .cons h (exec_of_along os _ hs)
192	
193	/-- Composition of sequences (§20.3 ¶3). -/
194	theorem run_append (s : Machine.State) (os os' : List (Machine.Op Ty)) :
195	    run s (os ++ os') = run (run s os) os' := by
196	  induction os generalizing s with
197	  | nil => rfl
198	  | cons o os ih => exact ih _
199	
200	/-- `Along` over a composed sequence (§20.3 ¶3). -/
201	theorem along_append {p : Machine.State → Machine.Op Ty → Prop} {s : Machine.State}
202	    {os os' : List (Machine.Op Ty)} :
203	    Along p s (os ++ os') ↔ Along p s os ∧ Along p (run s os) os' := by
204	  induction os generalizing s with
205	  | nil => simp [Along, run]
206	  | cons o os ih => simp only [List.cons_append, Along, run, ih, and_assoc]
207	
208	/-- Executions compose (§20.3 ¶3). -/
209	theorem exec_append {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty}
210	    {ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty} {os os' : List (Machine.Op Ty)} {s s' s'' : Machine.State}
211	    (h : Machine.Exec C ObR ObW os s s') (h' : Machine.Exec C ObR ObW os' s' s'') :
212	    Machine.Exec C ObR ObW (os ++ os') s s'' := by
213	  induction h with
214	  | nil => exact h'
215	  | cons hs _ ih => exact .cons hs (ih h')

219	/-! ## Allocations kept by raw operations (§13 ¶3, §16 ¶3, §17 ¶3) -/
220	
221	/-- `s'` keeps every allocation of `s` registered, with its base, size and deallocation token, and
222	every initialized byte initialized; liveness is not constrained (§13 ¶3, §16 ¶2, §16 ¶3,
223	§17 ¶3). -/
224	def Dom (s s' : Machine.State) : Prop :=
225	  ∀ i a, s.allocs i = some a → ∃ a', s'.allocs i = some a' ∧ a'.base = a.base ∧
226	    a'.size = a.size ∧ a'.freeAuth = a.freeAuth ∧ ∀ j, a.bytes j ≠ .uninit → a'.bytes j ≠ .uninit
227	
228	/-- `Dom` is reflexive (§13). -/
229	theorem Dom.refl (s : Machine.State) : Dom s s :=
230	  fun _ a h => ⟨a, h, rfl, rfl, rfl, fun _ h => h⟩
231	
232	/-- `Dom` is transitive (§13). -/
233	theorem Dom.trans {s s' s'' : Machine.State} (h : Dom s s') (h' : Dom s' s'') : Dom s s'' := by
234	  intro i a ha
235	  obtain ⟨a', ha', e1, e2, e3, hb⟩ := h i a ha
236	  obtain ⟨a'', ha'', f1, f2, f3, hb'⟩ := h' i a' ha'
237	  exact ⟨a'', ha'', f1.trans e1, f2.trans e2, f3.trans e3, fun j hj => hb' j (hb j hj)⟩
238	
239	/-- Transport of a property of a registered allocation along `Dom` (§13 ¶3). -/
240	theorem AllocP.dom {s s' : Machine.State} {i : Nat} {p : Machine.Alloc → Prop}
241	    (h : AllocP s i p) (hd : Dom s s')
242	    (hp : ∀ a a' : Machine.Alloc, a'.base = a.base → a'.size = a.size →
243	      a'.freeAuth = a.freeAuth → (∀ j, a.bytes j ≠ .uninit → a'.bytes j ≠ .uninit) →
244	      p a → p a') :
245	    AllocP s' i p := by
246	  obtain ⟨a, ha, hpa⟩ := h
247	  obtain ⟨a', ha', e1, e2, e3, hb⟩ := hd i a ha
248	  exact ⟨a', ha', hp a a' e1 e2 e3 hb hpa⟩
249	
250	/-- Initialized ranges stay initialized along `Dom` (§16 ¶2). -/
251	theorem AllocP.dom_init {s s' : Machine.State} {i off len : Nat}
252	    (h : AllocP s i fun a => a.InitRange off len) (hd : Dom s s') :
253	    AllocP s' i fun a => a.InitRange off len :=
254	  h.dom hd fun _ _ _ _ _ hb h j hj => hb _ (h j hj)
255	
256	/-- Allocation entries after a write (§16 ¶2, ¶3). -/
257	theorem write_allocs (s : Machine.State) (ac : Machine.Access) (w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat)
258	    (i : Nat) :
259	    (s.write ac w).allocs i = if i = ac.prov then
260	      (s.allocs i).map (fun a => a.write (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len w) else s.allocs i := rfl
261	
262	/-- Allocation entries after a deallocation (§17 ¶3). -/
263	theorem dealloc_allocs (s : Machine.State) (id i : Nat) :
264	    (s.dealloc id).allocs i = if i = id then
265	      (s.allocs i).map (fun a => { a with live := false }) else s.allocs i := rfl
266	
267	/-- Allocation entries after a creation (§9 ¶11, §13 ¶3). -/
268	theorem alloc_allocs (s : Machine.State) (sp b sz al : Nat) (fa : Option Nat) (i : Nat) :
269	    (s.alloc sp b sz al fa).allocs i = if i = s.next then
270	      some { space := sp, base := b, size := sz, align := al, live := true,
271	             bytes := fun _ => .uninit, freeAuth := fa } else s.allocs i := rfl

277	/-- Every `ok` effect keeps the allocations of a state with fresh identities (§13 ¶3, §16 ¶3,
278	§17 ¶3). -/
279	theorem dom_opEff {s : Machine.State} (hwf : Machine.WF s) (o : Machine.Op Ty) :
280	    Dom s (opEff o s) := by
281	  intro i a ha
282	  cases o with
283	  | read => exact ⟨a, ha, rfl, rfl, rfl, fun _ h => h⟩
284	  | write ac t w =>
285	    show ∃ a', (s.write ac w).allocs i = some a' ∧ _
286	    rw [write_allocs]
287	    split
288	    · refine ⟨a.write (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len w, by rw [ha]; simp, rfl, rfl, rfl, fun j hj => ?_⟩
289	      simp only [Machine.Alloc.write]
290	      split
291	      · exact fun h => by cases h
292	      · exact hj
293	    · exact ⟨a, ha, rfl, rfl, rfl, fun _ h => h⟩
294	  | dealloc id au =>
295	    show ∃ a', (s.dealloc id).allocs i = some a' ∧ _
296	    rw [dealloc_allocs]
297	    split
298	    · exact ⟨{ a with live := false }, by rw [ha]; simp, rfl, rfl, rfl, fun _ h => h⟩
299	    · exact ⟨a, ha, rfl, rfl, rfl, fun _ h => h⟩
300	  | alloc sp b sz al fa =>
301	    show ∃ a', (s.alloc sp b sz al fa).allocs i = some a' ∧ _
302	    have hi : i ≠ s.next := fun e => by rw [e, hwf s.next (Nat.le_refl _)] at ha; cases ha
303	    rw [alloc_allocs, ite_eq_right hi]
304	    exact ⟨a, ha, rfl, rfl, rfl, fun _ h => h⟩

306	/-- Every `ok` effect keeps freshness (§9 ¶7). -/
307	theorem wf_opEff {s : Machine.State} (hwf : Machine.WF s) (o : Machine.Op Ty) :
308	    Machine.WF (opEff o s) := by
309	  cases o with
310	  | read => exact hwf
311	  | write ac t w => exact Machine.write_wf hwf ac w
312	  | dealloc id au => exact Machine.dealloc_wf hwf id
313	  | alloc sp b sz al fa => exact Machine.alloc_wf hwf sp b sz al fa
314	
315	/-- Every sequence of `ok` effects keeps freshness (§9 ¶7). -/
316	theorem wf_run : ∀ (os : List (Machine.Op Ty)) (s : Machine.State), Machine.WF s →
317	    Machine.WF (run s os)
318	  | [], _, h => h
319	  | o :: os, _, h => wf_run os _ (wf_opEff h o)
320	
321	/-- Every sequence of `ok` effects keeps the allocations (§13 ¶3, §16 ¶3, §17 ¶3). -/
322	theorem dom_run : ∀ (os : List (Machine.Op Ty)) (s : Machine.State), Machine.WF s →
323	    Dom s (run s os)
324	  | [], s, _ => Dom.refl s
325	  | o :: os, _, h => (dom_opEff h o).trans (dom_run os _ (wf_opEff h o))

327	/-- An operation that deallocates no identity: a read, a write or a creation (§13 ¶3,
328	§16 ¶3). -/
329	def NoDealloc : Machine.Op Ty → Prop
330	  | .dealloc .. => False
331	  | _ => True

333	/-- An effect other than a deallocation keeps every live allocation live (§13 ¶3, §16 ¶3). -/
334	theorem live_opEff {s : Machine.State} (hwf : Machine.WF s) {o : Machine.Op Ty}
335	    (ho : NoDealloc o) {i : Nat} (h : LiveAlloc s i) : LiveAlloc (opEff o s) i := by
336	  obtain ⟨a, ha, hl⟩ := h
337	  cases o with
338	  | read => exact ⟨a, ha, hl⟩
339	  | write ac t w =>
340	    show AllocP (s.write ac w) i _
341	    rw [AllocP, write_allocs]
342	    split
343	    · exact ⟨a.write (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len w, by rw [ha]; simp, hl⟩
344	    · exact ⟨a, ha, hl⟩
345	  | dealloc => exact ho.elim
346	  | alloc sp b sz al fa =>
347	    have hi : i ≠ s.next := fun e => by rw [e, hwf s.next (Nat.le_refl _)] at ha; cases ha
348	    show AllocP (s.alloc sp b sz al fa) i _
349	    rw [AllocP, alloc_allocs, ite_eq_right hi]
350	    exact ⟨a, ha, hl⟩

353	theorem live_run : ∀ (os : List (Machine.Op Ty)) (s : Machine.State), Machine.WF s →
354	    (∀ o ∈ os, NoDealloc o) → ∀ {i : Nat}, LiveAlloc s i → LiveAlloc (run s os) i

356	  | o :: os, _, hwf, hn, _, h =>
357	    live_run os _ (wf_opEff hwf o) (fun o' ho' => hn o' (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ ho'))

363	    (h : AllocP s i fun _ => True) : baseOf (run s os) i = baseOf s i := by
364	  obtain ⟨a, ha, -⟩ := h

373	and same parents) and a memory state that keeps the allocations (`Dom`) and is admissible, when
374	every usable root place of the new state has a live allocation and every leaf that becomes `Init`
375	has its range initialized (§82.1, §82.3, §82.5). -/
376	theorem Repr.transport {L : Layout} {rtok : Nat → Nat} {s3 s3' : S3} {s2 s2' : Machine.State}
377	    (hR : Repr L rtok s3 s2) (hadm : Machine.Admissible s2') (hd : Dom s2 s2')
378	    (hlen : s3'.P.length = s3.P.length) (hpar : parentOf s3'.P = parentOf s3.P)
379	    (hlive : ∀ r, RootPlace s3.P r → s3'.Usable r → LiveAlloc s2' (L r).alloc)
380	    (hI : ∀ l, l < s3.P.length → isLeaf s3.P l → s3'.I l = .init →
381	      s3.I l = .init ∨ AllocP s2' (L l).alloc fun a => a.InitRange (L l).off (L l).len) :
382	    Repr L rtok s3' s2' := by
383	  have hleaf : ∀ l, isLeaf s3'.P l ↔ isLeaf s3.P l := fun l => by simp only [isLeaf, hlen, hpar]
384	  have hroot : ∀ r, RootPlace s3'.P r ↔ RootPlace s3.P r := fun r => by
385	    simp only [RootPlace, hlen, hpar]
386	  refine ⟨hadm, ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
387	  · intro q r h; rw [hpar] at h; exact hR.layout.parts q r h
388	  · intro l l' hl hl' hf hf' hne he
389	    rw [hlen] at hl hl'; rw [hleaf] at hf hf'
390	    exact hR.layout.disjoint l l' hl hl' hf hf' hne he
391	  · intro l hl hf
392	    rw [hlen] at hl; rw [hleaf] at hf
393	    exact (hR.layout.within l hl hf).dom hd fun _ _ _ e _ _ h => e ▸ h
394	  · intro r r' hr hr' hne
395	    exact hR.inj r r' ((hroot r).1 hr) ((hroot r').1 hr') hne
396	  · intro r hr
397	    exact (hR.tokens r ((hroot r).1 hr)).dom hd fun _ _ _ _ e _ h => e ▸ h
398	  · intro r hr hu
399	    exact hlive r ((hroot r).1 hr) hu
400	  · intro l hl hf hi
401	    rw [hlen] at hl; rw [hleaf] at hf
402	    rcases hI l hl hf hi with h | h
403	    · exact (hR.init l hl hf h).dom_init hd
404	    · exact h

489	/-- The reads realizing `read(access, ls)` (§82.2, §66): one raw read per leaf, of the range of
490	the leaf, at the type `ty l` of the leaf. -/
491	def readOps {Ty : Type} (s2 : Machine.State) (L : Layout) (ty : Nat → Ty) (ls : List Nat) :
492	    List (Machine.Op Ty) :=
493	  ls.map fun l => .read (leafAcc s2 L .read l) (ty l)

495	/-- Safe read (§82.2, §66, §15): under `Repr`, `WF3` and the preconditions of `read` (§66), the
496	raw read of the range of each leaf read is `ok` when the parametric obligations of that read hold
497	(§15.4, §15.6, §15.7): its allocation is live, the range is initialized, and the read returns the
498	bytes of the range. -/
499	theorem r1_read {Ty : Type} {ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty} {ty : Nat → Ty} {L : Layout}
500	    {rtok : Nat → Nat} {s3 : S3} {s2 : Machine.State} {a : Nat} {ls : List Nat}
501	    (hR : Repr L rtok s3 s2) (hw : WF3 s3) (hpre : Read3Pre s3 a ls) {l : Nat} (hl : l ∈ ls)
502	    (hob : ObR.dec s2 (leafAcc s2 L .read l) (ty l) ∧ ObR.stat s2 (leafAcc s2 L .read l) (ty l)) :
503	    ∃ al, s2.allocs (L l).alloc = some al ∧ al.live = true ∧ al.InitRange (L l).off (L l).len ∧
504	      Machine.ReadStep ObR (leafAcc s2 L .read l) (ty l) s2
505	        (.ok (al.bytesAt (L l).off (L l).len)) := by
506	  obtain ⟨hlP, hlf, hu⟩ := leaf_of_leafOfUsable hw (hpre.usable l hl)
507	  obtain ⟨al, hal, hlive, hsz⟩ := hR.leaf_live hw hlP hlf hu
508	  obtain ⟨al', hal', hi⟩ := hR.init l hlP hlf (hpre.init l hl)
509	  rw [hal] at hal'; cases hal'
510	  refine ⟨al, hal, hlive, hi, ?_⟩
511	  have hc := canRead_leaf hal hlive hsz hi
512	  have hst := Machine.ReadStep.ok (ObR := ObR) (t := ty l) hal ⟨hc, hob.1, hob.2⟩
513	  rw [leafAcc_of hal] at hst ⊢
514	  simpa only [Nat.add_sub_cancel_left] using hst

516	/-- The reads of a sequence of leaves leave the memory state unchanged (§20.2 ¶1). -/
517	theorem run_readOps {Ty : Type} (s2 : Machine.State) (L : Layout) (ty : Nat → Ty) :
518	    ∀ ls t, run t (readOps s2 L ty ls) = t
519	  | [], _ => rfl
520	  | _ :: ls, t => run_readOps s2 L ty ls t

522	/-- Realization of `read` (§82 preamble, §82.2, §66): under `Repr`, `WF3`, an `ok` step of `read`
523	and the parametric obligations along the reads, the reads form an execution of `ok` raw steps
524	that leaves the memory state unchanged, and `Repr` holds after the step. -/
525	theorem r6_read {Ty : Type} {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty}
526	    {ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty} {ty : Nat → Ty} {L : Layout} {rtok : Nat → Nat}
527	    {s3 s3' : S3} {s2 : Machine.State} {a : Nat} {ls : List Nat} (hR : Repr L rtok s3 s2)
528	    (hw : WF3 s3) (h : Read3Step a ls s3 (.ok s3'))
529	    (hob : OblAlong ObR ObW s2 (readOps s2 L ty ls)) :
530	    Machine.Exec C ObR ObW (readOps s2 L ty ls) s2 (run s2 (readOps s2 L ty ls)) ∧
531	      run s2 (readOps s2 L ty ls) = s2 ∧ Repr L rtok s3' (run s2 (readOps s2 L ty ls)) := by
532	  obtain ⟨hpre, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
533	  rw [run_readOps]
534	  refine ⟨?_, rfl, hR⟩
535	  have key : ∀ ls', (∀ l ∈ ls', l ∈ ls) → OblAlong ObR ObW s2 (readOps s2 L ty ls') →
536	      Along (OkAt C ObR ObW) s2 (readOps s2 L ty ls') := by
537	    intro ls'
538	    induction ls' with
539	    | nil => intro _ _; trivial
540	    | cons l ls' ih =>
541	      intro hsub hob'
542	      obtain ⟨al, hal, -, -, hst⟩ := r1_read hR hw hpre (hsub l (List.mem_cons_self ..)) hob'.1
543	      exact ⟨.read hst, ih (fun l' hl' => hsub l' (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hl')) hob'.2⟩
544	  have := exec_of_along _ _ (key ls (fun _ h => h) hob)
545	  rwa [run_readOps] at this

549	/-- `Repr` carries over a step that keeps the places and makes no place usable, along raw steps
550	that keep the allocations and every live allocation live (§82.1, §82.3, §82.5). -/
551	theorem Repr.same_places {L : Layout} {rtok : Nat → Nat} {s3 s3' : S3} {s2 s2' : Machine.State}
552	    (hR : Repr L rtok s3 s2) (hadm : Machine.Admissible s2') (hd : Dom s2 s2')
553	    (hl : ∀ i, LiveAlloc s2 i → LiveAlloc s2' i) (hP : s3'.P = s3.P)
554	    (hU : ∀ q, s3'.Usable q → s3.Usable q)
555	    (hI : ∀ l, l < s3.P.length → isLeaf s3.P l → s3'.I l = .init →
556	      s3.I l = .init ∨ AllocP s2' (L l).alloc fun a => a.InitRange (L l).off (L l).len) :
557	    Repr L rtok s3' s2' :=
558	  hR.transport hadm hd (by rw [hP]) (by rw [hP]) (fun r hr hu => hl _ (hR.live r hr (hU r hu))) hI
559

560	/-- `Repr` carries over a step that changes none of the places, the stack, the death markers and
561	the initialization states, with no raw operation (§82; §60–§62, §64, §74, §75: no storage
562	effect). -/

565	    (hI : s3'.I = s3.I) : Repr L rtok s3' s2 :=
566	  hR.same_places hR.adm (Dom.refl _) (fun _ h => h) hP (fun _ h => h.of_eqs hP hF hd)
567	    fun _ _ _ h => .inl (hI ▸ h)

569	/-! ## R2: safe writes (§82.2, §67, §68, §16) -/
570	
571	/-- The writes realizing `write(access, ls)` and `writeShared(access, ls)` (§82.2, §67, §68): one
572	raw write per leaf, of the range of the leaf, at the type `ty l`, of the representation `w l`
573	supplied by the program (§10 ¶4, §16 ¶2). -/
574	def writeOps {Ty : Type} (s2 : Machine.State) (L : Layout) (ty : Nat → Ty)
575	    (w : Nat → Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat) (ls : List Nat) : List (Machine.Op Ty) :=
576	  ls.map fun l => .write (leafAcc s2 L .write l) (ty l) (w l)
577	
578	/-- The writes of the ranges of leaves whose allocations are live and contain them are `ok` under
579	their parametric obligations (§16, §82.2), and afterwards every written range is initialized
580	(§16 ¶2). -/
581	theorem writes_ok {Ty : Type} {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty}
582	    {ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty} {L : Layout} {ty : Nat → Ty}
583	    {w : Nat → Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat} :
584	    ∀ (ls : List Nat) (s2 : Machine.State), Machine.WF s2 →
585	      (∀ l ∈ ls, AllocP s2 (L l).alloc fun a => a.live = true ∧ (L l).off + (L l).len ≤ a.size) →
586	      OblAlong ObR ObW s2 (writeOps s2 L ty w ls) →
587	      Along (OkAt C ObR ObW) s2 (writeOps s2 L ty w ls) ∧
588	        ∀ l ∈ ls, AllocP (run s2 (writeOps s2 L ty w ls)) (L l).alloc
589	          fun a => a.InitRange (L l).off (L l).len
590	  | [], _, _, _, _ => ⟨trivial, fun _ h => nomatch h⟩
591	  | l :: ls, s2, hwf, hls, hob => by
592	    obtain ⟨al, hal, hlive, hsz⟩ := hls l (List.mem_cons_self ..)
593	    have hex : AllocP s2 (L l).alloc fun _ => True := ⟨al, hal, trivial⟩
594	    have hd₁ : Dom s2 (s2.write (leafAcc s2 L .write l) (w l)) :=
595	      dom_opEff (Ty := Ty) hwf (.write (leafAcc s2 L .write l) (ty l) (w l))
596	    have hwf₁ : Machine.WF (s2.write (leafAcc s2 L .write l) (w l)) :=
597	      Machine.write_wf hwf _ _
598	    have hops : writeOps (s2.write (leafAcc s2 L .write l) (w l)) L ty w ls =
599	        writeOps s2 L ty w ls := by
600	      simp only [writeOps, List.map_inj_left]
601	      intro l' hl'
602	      obtain ⟨b, hb, -⟩ := hls l' (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hl')
603	      rw [leafAcc_dom hd₁ ⟨b, hb, trivial⟩]
604	    have hls₁ : ∀ l' ∈ ls, AllocP (s2.write (leafAcc s2 L .write l) (w l)) (L l').alloc
605	        fun a => a.live = true ∧ (L l').off + (L l').len ≤ a.size := by
606	      intro l' hl'
607	      obtain ⟨b, hb, hbl, hbs⟩ := hls l' (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hl')
608	      obtain ⟨b', hb', -, e, -⟩ := hd₁ _ b hb
609	      refine ⟨b', hb', ?_, e ▸ hbs⟩
610	      have := live_opEff (Ty := Ty) (o := .write (leafAcc s2 L .write l) (ty l) (w l)) hwf trivial
611	        ⟨b, hb, hbl⟩
612	      obtain ⟨b'', hb'', hl''⟩ := this
613	      change (s2.write (leafAcc s2 L .write l) (w l)).allocs _ = _ at hb''
614	      rw [hb'] at hb''; cases hb''; exact hl''
615	    have hob₁ : OblAlong ObR ObW (s2.write (leafAcc s2 L .write l) (w l))
616	        (writeOps (s2.write (leafAcc s2 L .write l) (w l)) L ty w ls) := by
617	      rw [hops]; exact hob.2
618	    obtain ⟨ih1, ih2⟩ := writes_ok (C := C) ls _ hwf₁ hls₁ hob₁
619	    rw [hops] at ih1 ih2
620	    refine ⟨⟨.write (.ok ⟨canWrite_leaf hal hlive hsz, hob.1⟩), ih1⟩, fun l' hl' => ?_⟩
621	    rcases List.mem_cons.1 hl' with rfl | hl'
622	    · exact (write_leaf_init hex).dom_init (dom_run _ _ hwf₁)
623	    · exact ih2 l' hl'
624	
625	/-- The writes form no deallocation (§16). -/
626	theorem writeOps_noDealloc {Ty : Type} (s2 : Machine.State) (L : Layout) (ty : Nat → Ty)
627	    (w : Nat → Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat) (ls : List Nat) :
628	    ∀ o ∈ writeOps s2 L ty w ls, NoDealloc o := by
629	  intro o ho
630	  obtain ⟨l, -, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.1 ho
631	  trivial

633	/-- Realization of the writes of a step whose written leaves belong to usable places, which keeps
634	the places, the stack and the death markers, and makes `Init` only written leaves (§82.2, §82.3,
635	§67, §68, §65, §16): the raw writes are `ok` and `Repr` holds after the step. -/
636	theorem writes_repr {Ty : Type} {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty}
637	    {ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty} {ty : Nat → Ty} {w : Nat → Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat}
638	    {L : Layout} {rtok : Nat → Nat} {s3 s3' : S3} {s2 : Machine.State} {ls : List Nat}
639	    (hR : Repr L rtok s3 s2) (hw : WF3 s3) (hu : ∀ l ∈ ls, LeafOfUsable s3 l)
640	    (hob : OblAlong ObR ObW s2 (writeOps s2 L ty w ls)) (hP : s3'.P = s3.P) (hF : s3'.F = s3.F)
641	    (hd : s3'.dead = s3.dead) (hI : ∀ l, s3'.I l = .init → s3.I l = .init ∨ l ∈ ls) :
642	    Machine.Exec C ObR ObW (writeOps s2 L ty w ls) s2 (run s2 (writeOps s2 L ty w ls)) ∧
643	      Repr L rtok s3' (run s2 (writeOps s2 L ty w ls)) := by
644	  have hls : ∀ l ∈ ls, AllocP s2 (L l).alloc
645	      fun a => a.live = true ∧ (L l).off + (L l).len ≤ a.size := fun l hl => by
646	    obtain ⟨hlP, hlf, hu⟩ := leaf_of_leafOfUsable hw (hu l hl)
647	    exact hR.leaf_live hw hlP hlf hu
648	  obtain ⟨hok, hinit⟩ := writes_ok (C := C) ls s2 hR.adm.wf hls hob
649	  have hex := exec_of_along _ _ hok
650	  refine ⟨hex, hR.same_places (hex.admissible hR.adm) (dom_run _ _ hR.adm.wf)
651	    (fun _ h => live_run _ _ hR.adm.wf (writeOps_noDealloc s2 L ty w ls) h) hP
652	    (fun _ h => h.of_eqs hP hF hd) fun l _ _ hi => ?_⟩
653	  rcases hI l hi with h | h
654	  · exact .inl h
655	  · exact .inr (hinit l h)

582	    {ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty} {L : Layout} {ty : Nat → Ty}
583	    {w : Nat → Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat} :
584	    ∀ (ls : List Nat) (s2 : Machine.State), Machine.WF s2 →
585	      (∀ l ∈ ls, AllocP s2 (L l).alloc fun a => a.live = true ∧ (L l).off + (L l).len ≤ a.size) →
586	      OblAlong ObR ObW s2 (writeOps s2 L ty w ls) →
587	      Along (OkAt C ObR ObW) s2 (writeOps s2 L ty w ls) ∧
588	        ∀ l ∈ ls, AllocP (run s2 (writeOps s2 L ty w ls)) (L l).alloc
589	          fun a => a.InitRange (L l).off (L l).len
590	  | [], _, _, _, _ => ⟨trivial, fun _ h => nomatch h⟩
591	  | l :: ls, s2, hwf, hls, hob => by
592	    obtain ⟨al, hal, hlive, hsz⟩ := hls l (List.mem_cons_self ..)
593	    have hex : AllocP s2 (L l).alloc fun _ => True := ⟨al, hal, trivial⟩
594	    have hd₁ : Dom s2 (s2.write (leafAcc s2 L .write l) (w l)) :=

596	    have hwf₁ : Machine.WF (s2.write (leafAcc s2 L .write l) (w l)) :=
597	      Machine.write_wf hwf _ _

601	      intro l' hl'
602	      obtain ⟨b, hb, -⟩ := hls l' (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hl')
603	      rw [leafAcc_dom hd₁ ⟨b, hb, trivial⟩]

605	        fun a => a.live = true ∧ (L l').off + (L l').len ≤ a.size := by
606	      intro l' hl'
607	      obtain ⟨b, hb, hbl, hbs⟩ := hls l' (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hl')
608	      obtain ⟨b', hb', -, e, -⟩ := hd₁ _ b hb
609	      refine ⟨b', hb', ?_, e ▸ hbs⟩
610	      have := live_opEff (Ty := Ty) (o := .write (leafAcc s2 L .write l) (ty l) (w l)) hwf trivial
611	        ⟨b, hb, hbl⟩
612	      obtain ⟨b'', hb'', hl''⟩ := this
613	      change (s2.write (leafAcc s2 L .write l) (w l)).allocs _ = _ at hb''
614	      rw [hb'] at hb''; cases hb''; exact hl''
615	    have hob₁ : OblAlong ObR ObW (s2.write (leafAcc s2 L .write l) (w l))

617	      rw [hops]; exact hob.2
618	    obtain ⟨ih1, ih2⟩ := writes_ok (C := C) ls _ hwf₁ hls₁ hob₁
619	    rw [hops] at ih1 ih2
620	    refine ⟨⟨.write (.ok ⟨canWrite_leaf hal hlive hsz, hob.1⟩), ih1⟩, fun l' hl' => ?_⟩
621	    rcases List.mem_cons.1 hl' with rfl | hl'
622	    · exact (write_leaf_init hex).dom_init (dom_run _ _ hwf₁)
623	    · exact ih2 l' hl'

`lsimulation`), in which `issue` is the derived library operation (`split` then `store`) and
`reset` the derived reset (`derive` then `release`). The reached states are those of these runs
(material §0, rule 3). The obtained result is stated with the kernel relation of the step under
test, the machine relations of its realized raw operations (`ReadStep`, `WriteStep`,
`DeallocStep`, `Exec`) and the bytes read back, all decided by `decide`.

Each docstring gives the expected verdict of the material, the obtained one, the class (material
§0, rule 5: `R` refinement) and the positive twin of each rejection or `fail` (rule 2). A case
whose obtained verdict differs from its expected one, or whose expected verdict has no spec v0
source, is kept with its expected verdict and classified; no case is corrected.

Address rules of references (decisions of the brief, recorded for §82.3 in `Refinement.ptrAddr`):
an empty region has the base of the allocation of its effective anchor, with that allocation as
provenance; a nonempty region has the lowest address among its leaves of nonzero size; the
destination leaf has the size of a reference (`pe8.size = 8`).

Not encoded (classified, material §3 and §6):
* MM23-H14, a raw pointer formed before a call and used during the call on the footprint of a
  `Modify` parameter: undefined behavior that no safe program constructs; class spec 3 (strong
  protection of parameters during the invocation, §72 last paragraph, §81) with the boundary of
  §19 (reconstruction of accesses from raw addresses).
* MM23-H17, a reference stored into a leaf of zero size: a conditional obligation of specs 4 and
  11 (a reference occupies a leaf of pointer size), not a guarantee of the refinement; class
  specs 4 and 11 (§81, §82.3 "a single logical leaf with an appropriate representation"). The
  pointer-size rule is a hypothesis of `Refinement.pointer_sound_store`.
-/

1508	/-- Geometry of a new allocation: address space, size, alignment (§9 ¶1). -/
1509	structure Geom where
1510	  /-- §9 ¶1: address space. -/

1512	  /-- §9 ¶1: extent in bytes. -/

1517	/-- Placement: the base address chosen for a new allocation of geometry `g` in the state `s`
1518	(§9 ¶11, §82.4). -/

1521	/-- Obligation of a placement (§9 ¶11, §82.4): in every state with fresh identities, for every
1522	valid alignment, the chosen base satisfies the preconditions of raw creation. -/
1523	def PlacementOK (pl : Placement) : Prop :=
1524	  ∀ s g, Machine.WF s → 0 < g.align → Machine.Pow2 g.align →
1525	    Machine.AllocPre s g.space (pl s g) g.size g.align
1526	
1527	/-- Obligation of the geometries (§9 ¶1, ¶4): every alignment is strictly positive and a power of
1528	two. -/
1529	def GeomOK (g : Nat → Geom) : Prop := ∀ r, 0 < (g r).align ∧ Machine.Pow2 (g r).align

1531	/-- End of the allocation `i` of `s`, `0` if unregistered (§9 ¶3). -/
1532	def allocEnd (s : Machine.State) (i : Nat) : Nat :=
1533	  ((s.allocs i).map fun a => a.base + a.size).getD 0
1534	
1535	/-- Largest end of the allocations of identity below `n` (§9 ¶3). -/
1536	def maxEnd (s : Machine.State) : Nat → Nat
1537	  | 0 => 0
1538	  | n + 1 => max (maxEnd s n) (allocEnd s n)
1539	
1540	/-- Every allocation below `n` ends at most at `maxEnd s n` (§9 ¶3). -/
1541	theorem le_maxEnd (s : Machine.State) : ∀ n i, i < n → allocEnd s i ≤ maxEnd s n
1542	  | 0, _, h => absurd h (Nat.not_lt_zero _)
1543	  | n + 1, i, h => by
1544	    simp only [maxEnd]
1545	    rcases Nat.lt_succ_iff_lt_or_eq.1 h with h | rfl
1546	    · exact Nat.le_trans (le_maxEnd s n i h) (Nat.le_max_left _ _)
1547	    · exact Nat.le_max_right _ _

1549	/-- A placement above every registered allocation, on a multiple of the alignment (§9 ¶11; a
1550	witness that `PlacementOK` is satisfiable, `topPlacement_ok`). -/
1551	def topPlacement : Placement := fun s g => g.align * (maxEnd s s.next / g.align + 1)
1552	
1553	/-- `topPlacement` satisfies its obligation (§9 ¶11, §82.4). -/
1554	theorem topPlacement_ok : PlacementOK topPlacement := by
1555	  intro s g hwf h0 h2
1556	  refine ⟨hwf _ (Nat.le_refl _), h0, h2, Nat.mul_mod_right _ _, fun i a ha _ _ => ?_⟩
1557	  have hi : i < s.next := Nat.lt_of_not_le fun hle => by rw [hwf i hle] at ha; cases ha
1558	  have he : a.base + a.size ≤ maxEnd s s.next := by
1559	    have := le_maxEnd s s.next i hi; simpa [allocEnd, ha] using this
1560	  have hb := Nat.lt_mul_div_succ (maxEnd s s.next) h0
1561	  exact Machine.rangeDisjoint_iff.2 (.inl (by simp only [topPlacement]; omega))

1563	/-- Justification of `Satisfiable` on the side of the memory machine (§82.4, §71, §9): addresses
1564	are unbounded naturals in this kernel (§9 ¶6), so every allocation of valid alignment has a valid

1566	the provider's contract, never from the machine; address width belongs to §81 (Spec 11). -/

1572	appended after `n` places, in order, one allocation of geometry `g (n + i)` at the base chosen by
1573	`pl`, recording the token `rtok (n + i)`. -/

1575	    Machine.State → List Nat → List (Machine.Op Ty)

1577	  | s, i :: is => .alloc (g (n + i)).space (pl s (g (n + i))) (g (n + i)).size (g (n + i)).align
1578	      (some (rtok (n + i))) :: allocOps pl g rtok n (s.alloc (g (n + i)).space (pl s (g (n + i)))

1585	/-- The creations are `ok` under the placement and geometry obligations (§9 ¶11). -/

1591	  | _ :: is, s, h =>

1596	theorem allocOps_old : ∀ (is : List Nat) (s : Machine.State) (i : Nat), i < s.next →

1598	  | [], _, _, _ => rfl
1599	  | _ :: is, s, i, hi => by
1600	    show (run (s.alloc _ _ _ _ _) (allocOps pl g rtok n _ is)).allocs i = _
1601	    rw [allocOps_old is _ i (by simp only [Machine.State.alloc]; omega)]

1604	/-- The `j`-th creation registers the identity `next + j`, live, uninitialized, with the geometry
1605	of its root and its token (§9 ¶11, §10 ¶5, §13 ¶1). -/
1606	theorem allocOps_new : ∀ (is : List Nat) (s : Machine.State) (j i : Nat), is[j]? = some i →
1607	    ∃ b, (run s (allocOps (Ty := Ty) pl g rtok n s is)).allocs (s.next + j) =
1608	      some ⟨(g (n + i)).space, b, (g (n + i)).size, (g (n + i)).align, true, fun _ => .uninit,
1609	        some (rtok (n + i))⟩
1610	  | [], _, _, _, h => by simp at h
1611	  | k :: is, s, 0, i, h => by
1612	    simp only [List.getElem?_cons_zero, Option.some.injEq] at h; subst h
1613	    refine ⟨pl s (g (n + k)), ?_⟩
1614	    show (run (s.alloc _ _ _ _ _) (allocOps pl g rtok n _ is)).allocs _ = _
1615	    rw [allocOps_old pl g rtok n is _ _ (by simp [Machine.State.alloc])]
1616	    simp [Machine.State.alloc]
1617	  | k :: is, s, j + 1, i, h => by
1618	    simp only [List.getElem?_cons_succ] at h
1619	    obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := allocOps_new is (s.alloc (g (n + k)).space (pl s (g (n + k)))
1620	      (g (n + k)).size (g (n + k)).align (some (rtok (n + k)))) j i h
1621	    refine ⟨b, ?_⟩
1622	    show (run (s.alloc _ _ _ _ _) (allocOps pl g rtok n _ is)).allocs _ = _

1631	  | _, _ :: is, o, h => by
1632	    rcases List.mem_cons.1 h with rfl | h
1633	    · trivial
1634	    · exact allocOps_noDealloc _ is o h

2216	  | write => exact r2_write hR hw h hob
2217	  | writeShared => exact r2_writeShared hR hw h hob

2219	  | unpin => exact ⟨.nil _, r6_unpin hR h⟩
2220	  | endUse => exact ⟨.nil _, r6_endUse hR h⟩

2272	`exitRoots` is usable before the exit and not after. -/

2275	    s3.Usable r ∧ ¬ ({ s3 with F := s3.F.tail } : S3).Usable r := by
2276	  obtain ⟨hrt, ho, hd⟩ := mem_exitRoots.1 hr
2277	  cases hpl : s3.P[r]? with
2278	  | none => rw [hpl] at ho; exact ho.elim
2279	  | some pl =>
2280	    rw [hpl] at ho; simp only [OptP] at ho
2281	    refine ⟨.frame hpl hd ho (top_mem hF), fun hu => ?_⟩
2282	    cases hu with
2283	    | frame hpl' _ ho' hf =>
2284	      change s3.P[r]? = some _ at hpl'
2285	      rw [hpl] at hpl'; cases hpl'; rw [ho] at ho'; cases ho'
2286	      have hnd := hw.frames.2.1
2287	      have ht : s3.top ∈ s3.F.tail := hf
2288	      unfold S3.top at ht
2289	      cases hFe : s3.F with
2290	      | nil => exact hF hFe
2291	      | cons f F => rw [hFe] at ht hnd; exact (List.nodup_cons.1 hnd).1 ht
2292	    | place hpl' _ ho' _ =>
2293	      change s3.P[r]? = some _ at hpl'
2294	      rw [hpl] at hpl'; cases hpl'; rw [ho] at ho'; cases ho'

2684	/-- A successful translated run extends a `SimRun` (§82 preamble). -/
2685	theorem srun_sound {k : K} [∀ r r', Decidable (k.DeclaredDisjoint r r')]
2686	    [DecidablePred k.SharedMutable] [DecidablePred k.Pinned] [DecidablePred k.ExternalDone]
2687	    [DecidablePred k.Deallocable] [∀ p a, Decidable (k.FreeCompat p a)]
2688	    [∀ p ls s, Decidable (k.Satisfiable p ls s)] {Ty : Type} {C : Nat → Nat → Prop}
2689	    [DecidableRel C] {ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty} {ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty}
2690	    [∀ s o, Decidable (Obl ObR ObW s o)] {π : Params Ty} {statics : Statics} :
2691	    ∀ (ops : List KOp) (st st' : S3 × Machine.State),
2692	      SimRun k C ObR ObW statics π st.1 st.2 → srun k C ObR ObW π st ops = some st' →
2693	      SimRun k C ObR ObW statics π st'.1 st'.2
2694	  | [], st, st', h, he => by
2695	    simp only [srun, Option.some.injEq] at he; subst he; exact h
2696	  | op :: ops, st, st', h, he => by
2697	    simp only [srun] at he
2698	    cases hs : sstep k C ObR ObW π st op with
2699	    | none => rw [hs] at he; cases he
2700	    | some st₁ =>
2701	      rw [hs] at he
2702	      simp only [Option.bind_some] at he
2703	      unfold sstep at hs
2704	      split at hs
2705	      · rename_i hc
2706	        simp only [Option.some.injEq] at hs; subst hs
2707	        exact srun_sound ops _ st' (.step h (wf3_of_check hc.1) (noDangling_of_check hc.2.1)
2708	          (opStep_of_pre hc.2.2.1) hc.2.2.2) he
2709	      · cases hs

2727	/-- Root place of `q`: the last element of its parent chain (§40). -/
2728	def rootOf (P : List Place) (q : Nat) : Nat := (chain (parentOf P) q).getLastD q

2730	/-- Number of root places below `r`: the identity of the allocation of the root `r` when every root
2731	place receives one allocation in index order (§9 ¶11, §82.1). -/
2732	def rootRank (P : List Place) (r : Nat) : Nat :=
2733	  ((List.range r).filter fun i => decide (i < P.length ∧ parentOf P i = none)).length
2734	
2735	/-- Number of leaves of the root of `l` below `l` (§82.1). -/
2736	def leafRank (P : List Place) (l : Nat) : Nat :=
2737	  ((List.range l).filter fun i => decide (isLeaf P i ∧ rootOf P i = rootOf P l)).length

2739	/-- Test layout for the places `P` (§82.1): a place in the allocation of its root; a leaf of 8
2740	bytes at 8 times its rank among the leaves of its root; leaves of the roots listed in `z` have
2741	size zero (§71.1, zero physical size). -/
2742	def autoL (P : List Place) (z : List Nat) : Layout := fun q =>
2743	  if rootOf P q ∈ z then ⟨rootRank P (rootOf P q), 0, 0⟩
2744	  else ⟨rootRank P (rootOf P q), 8 * leafRank P q, 8⟩
2745	
2746	/-- Test geometry (§9 ¶1): 8 bytes per leaf of the root, aligned on 8; size zero for the roots of
2747	`z`. -/
2748	def autoG (P : List Place) (z : List Nat) : Nat → Geom := fun r =>
2749	  if r ∈ z then ⟨0, 0, 8⟩ else ⟨0, 8 * (footprint P r).length, 8⟩
2750	
2751	/-- The test geometry has valid alignments (§9 ¶4). -/
2752	theorem autoG_ok (P : List Place) (z : List Nat) : GeomOK (autoG P z) := fun r => by
2753	  simp only [autoG]; split <;> exact ⟨Nat.succ_pos 7, 3, rfl⟩

2755	/-- Test reference encoding (§82.3): 8 bytes, little-endian, each with the provenance. -/
2756	def pe8 : PtrEnc where
2757	  size := 8
2758	  enc addr prov i := ((addr / 256 ^ i % 256).toUInt8, prov)
2759	  decode f := (List.range 8).foldr (fun i acc => acc + (f i).1.toNat * 256 ^ i) 0
2760	  reads f g h := by
2761	    have key : ∀ l : List Nat, (∀ i ∈ l, i < 8) →
2762	        l.foldr (fun i acc => acc + (f i).1.toNat * 256 ^ i) 0 =
2763	          l.foldr (fun i acc => acc + (g i).1.toNat * 256 ^ i) 0 := by
2764	      intro l hl
2765	      induction l with
2766	      | nil => rfl
2767	      | cons a l ih =>
2768	        simp only [List.foldr_cons]
2769	        rw [ih fun i hi => hl i (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hi), h a (hl a (List.mem_cons_self ..))]
2770	    exact key _ fun i hi => List.mem_range.1 hi

def I1 (s : S3) : Prop :=

authority is valid, that is, active. -/

## 80. Parametric Contracts of the Access Discipline

A contract `K` parameterizes rules of the access discipline without fabricating permissions. A safe abstraction using part of `K` must prove or fulfill the corresponding obligation; an unestablished precondition is not a language guarantee.

| Contract | External obligation |
|---|---|
| `DeclaredDisjoint` | `DDSound(K)`: no falsely declared disjoint region when leaves can overlap |
| `Pinned` | I5, prohibition of incompatible physical moves; `StaticPinnedBottom` for pinned statics |
| `SharedMutable` | Applicable shared-mutation discipline, with correct rights and synchronization |
| `ExternalDone` | External use of storage has ended when `unpin` is permitted |
| `Deallocable` | The place belongs to a unit that can actually be freed |
| `FreeCompat` | Opaque deallocation authority is compatible with the unit being freed |
| `Satisfiable` | The provider can satisfy the requested shape **in the current state** |

Structural conditions of `free`, dependencies, and the derived library `reset` carry the relevant invalidation obligations. Physical justification of `DDSound` must be established by a realization consistent with memory layouts and Section 82.

## 81. Boundaries Remaining to Be Specified
## 70. O13 — Release of an Owned Storage Unit

**Preconditions**

1. `place` is a **root of storage owned by a value** (`OwnedRoot`), not an ordinary local directly owned by a frame and not part of an aggregate.
2. `K.Deallocable(place)` is established, and `K.FreeCompat(place,auth)` justifies deallocation authority `auth`; this identifier is opaque to the authority kernel.
3. The current frame has exercisable `Modify`; no active derivative over the footprint being freed is held outside holders that die; no surviving place is anchored to an authority of the released region or of its dead holders. The authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right over `place`, namely the exercisable authority on which that right rests and its origin chain, are exempt from the check on active derivatives. Moreover, no authority that the effect makes inactive (an authority of the released region, its root included, or an authority whose holder dies) has an active descendant, whatever its footprint, that the same step does not make inactive.
4. No leaf of the released unit is statically or dynamically pinned. Ending external use does not silently turn a still-pinned leaf into a releasable unit.

**`ok` effect:** `place` and the storage that ceases to live are marked dead; authorities of those regions, including their corresponding roots, become inactive, as do authorities whose holders die. Surviving dependencies must remain valid. Every realization of `free` must satisfy the corresponding deallocation relation of the elementary memory machine (Part III). **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 71. O14 — Allocation of a New Storage Root

**Static preconditions**

1. `shape` is a **nonempty** abstract shape, represented like the local places of `enterFrame`; an allocation of **zero physical size** may be represented by a logical one-leaf shape.
2. The provider is a usable place, and **all leaves of the provider** are `Init`; updates to its metadata are permitted through exercisable `Modify` or a valid `writeShared` over `SharedMutable` metadata.
3. The current frame has exercisable `Modify` over `owner`; new identities and ownership relations must respect `WF3`, `RootHeld`, and liveness restrictions.

**Outcomes**

- `reject`: a static precondition does not hold;
- `fail`: static preconditions hold, but `K.Satisfiable(provider,shape,s)` is false in the state under consideration; **no state change**;
- `ok(s')`: creation of a **new storage root** with fresh identity, owned by `owner`; its leaves start `Uninit`, its new root `Modify` authority with no origin is held by `owner`; provider metadata is updated only in accordance with its modification rights.

Allocation success depends on the provider's state: it does not constitute a right to invent physical memory. Any realization of this operation must satisfy the `AllocStep` relation defined by the rules of Sections 9 and 13.

# XII. Call Frames and Return of Authorities
## 65. O8 — Controlled Storage of an Authority

**Preconditions**

1. `authority` is active, **derived**, and held by the current frame; a root authority can never be stored by `store`.
2. `target` is a usable **leaf** under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame. It holds no other **active** authority. Its data already being `Init` does not by itself prohibit the operation.
3. The stored authority covers neither a leaf of `target` nor the leaves of storage transitively owned by it.
4. The effective anchor of `authority` respects `AnchorOrder` relative to the frame of `target`; other dependencies are preserved.
5. **In the resulting state**, `target` remains under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame (`store_keeps_target_reachable`), and `AnchorOrderHeld` remains true. This is a genuine additional precondition, not an automatic consequence of the preceding ones.

**`ok` effect:** The holder of `authority` becomes `target`; the authority is added to `D(target)`; **only** leaf `target` becomes `Init`. Other fields of a structure, even adjacent ones, do not change their initialization state. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

Overwriting an active authority already held by the leaf is prohibited; its explicit release may make the target reusable. The resulting-state clause does not by itself prohibit all cycles possible after other operations: general freedom from blocking (`NoLock`) is not adopted here.

# X. Reading, Writing, and Initialization

19:Raw memory-model operations are interpreted by **transition relations**. Their role is to determine the semantic outcome without assuming that all their obligations can be computed at runtime. Operation names are semantic designations independent of any particular implementation or formalization.
23:- a raw operation satisfying all applicable obligations has a defined `ok` outcome with the specified effect;
24:- violation of a safety obligation of that operation produces a `ub` outcome (Section 6), **including when the obligation is static**;
27:Memory-machine relations may be deterministic and mathematically total even when certain obligations are not constructively decidable. A classical proof of totality is not a runtime requirement. Modeling a defined failure of resource reservation belongs to the allocator contract: it does not change the classification of violations of safety obligations of raw operations.
31:A valid **byte read** does not modify memory state; its `ok` outcome supplies the sequence of abstract bytes actually read, including provenance. A raw typed read must additionally satisfy type, alignment, and concurrency obligations and subsequent value-reconstruction rules. Unlike operations that only transition the state, a read supplies a value together with its successful outcome.
35:### 20.3 — Parametric Obligations and Executions
37:Read and write obligations not yet concretely defined are **explicit predicates** of the semantic context: they are not tacitly replaced by `True`.
41:A normative relation requires **no decision instance** for these predicates to be stated. A computable function may require a decision instance for conditions it evaluates. Obligations and the deallocation-compatibility relation are fixed as **parameters of an execution's context**; obligation predicates may nevertheless depend on the state and operation. The minimal compatibility relation of Section 17 concerns the presented authority and the deallocation token; additional state-dependent contracts belong to the relevant abstraction.
53:Stability of **observed contents** is not guaranteed for leaves whose storage is declared `SharedMutable` when permitted shared-mutation operations may execute. This exception removes neither structural exclusivity I1 nor authority-validity obligations. Likewise, a region declared as susceptible to external modification does not benefit from ordinary content stability; its particular guarantees are declared by the storage and its contract. Pinning (`Pinned`) may preserve an address without guaranteeing stability of the data at that address.
67:This capability is modeled by the kernel operation `split` (Section 61, O2). Disjointness may be structurally guaranteed, statically proved, or justified by a prior dynamic check encapsulated in a safe abstraction, including correctly justified internal unsafe operations. For `DeclaredDisjoint`, the normative condition is **leaf disjointness**; under a memory layout satisfying `LayoutWF`, it implies disjointness of the corresponding bytes. Merely asserting disjointness without justification does not authorize splitting.
